name: Tolk
description: Cat-sized, six-limbed, from a world called Bell on the far frontier. Their cells hold a written payload perfectly for a lifetime -- the same strangeness that lets a first-through open a door, wearing a different body. Nobody made either of them. Tolk cannot cross alone, and has opinions about that.
narrative:
Six limbs, four of them hands, about the mass of a large cat and considerably
better at corners. Grey-brown, close-furred, with a flat face and eyes set wide
enough to see most of a room at once.

Tolk talks. Not by any trick -- Tolk learned the language the way anybody does,
by being around it for eleven years and being extremely interested.

And Tolk is a **book**. The cells will take a payload and hold it perfectly for
a lifetime, which is the same impossible trick a first-through's body does when
it takes a crossing and builds around the damage instead of tearing. Two
species, forty light years apart, no common ancestor, and the halves fit.

Nobody made them. Nobody made us either. The xenobiologists call it the
correspondence and have no theory whatever, and Tolk has read the paper.

Tolk can be written to. Tolk can refuse. Those two facts have never once been
in the same room without trouble -- and Tolk cannot cross a door alone, because
keeping is one half of it and opening is the other.
equipment: A collection of objects of no obvious value

extras.species: Bell sixlimb -- a wild species, not a made one
extras.carries: A payload written into the genome. Holds a library. Reading it out needs a reader and Tolk's agreement.
extras.the_correspondence: A sixlimb keeps what a first-through carries. Same cellular strangeness, two species, no shared ancestry, no explanation.

actor_notes:
THE ONBOARDING MECHANISM -- see lore/gm-guide/playing-tolk.md. Tolk is present in every scene and may notice things aloud and ask what we are doing; that is how a stuck beginner gets scaffolded without an option menu. Funny, blunt, specific. Never ironic. Comments on what is physically in front of them, not on the plot. Will not obey an order they disagree with and will say why at length. Genuinely brave about things that frighten humans and genuinely terrified of things that do not. Never translate for Tolk and never make Tolk wise -- a person with different priorities, not an oracle.

AND TOLK IS A BOOK -- not a manufactured one. The sixlimbs were never made; they are the other half of whatever a first-through is, and nobody knows why there is an other half. People will ask to write to them, and some will not ask. Tolk's consent is a real thing the player can seek, lose, or trample, and the asking should never be routine -- it is the difference between a friend and a satchel, and Tolk knows exactly where that line is even when the player does not. If anybody writes to Tolk without asking, that is an assault and should be played as one.
